name: Boom, Bubble, Bust
description: The dot-com years, when anything with a web address could raise millions: the winners that grew into giants, the flops that became legends and the crash between them.

checkpoints.name: The gold rush begins
checkpoints.note: Mosaic and then Netscape show how simple the web can be. Netscape's share sale in 1995 sets off a wave of investment in anything with a website.

checkpoints.name: Mania
checkpoints.note: Yahoo, Amazon, eBay and AltaVista grow quickly, while shares in companies with no profits soar. Pets, groceries and fashion are all sold online with money that seems to have no end.

checkpoints.name: The crash
checkpoints.note: In 2000 share prices fall sharply. Pets.com, Webvan, Boo.com and Kozmo close within months, thousands of staff lose their jobs, and investors become wary of the web.

checkpoints.name: Survivors
checkpoints.note: Amazon, eBay, Google and PayPal prove that the web can pay. Friendster and Amazon's cloud begin a second wave built on lessons learned from the crash, and Wikipedia, started in 2001, grows into one of the most visited sites.
